verdict.rationale: Svelte is a compiler-based UI framework, so it does not itself accept natural-language commands. It does ship its own AI-facing tooling: an official MCP server that helps an agent write Svelte code by supplying relevant documentation and statically analysing the generated code, plus LLM-oriented llms.txt documentation. This lets a user drive Svelte development through natural-language prompts to an agent, but only indirectly. Missing for 10: direct natural-language operation of the product or its CLI, documentation of end-to-end natural-language workflows (e.g. scaffolding or adding features by prompt), and independent or hands-on corroboration that the MCP-assisted flow works.
